header: Pages as cards, one line each
lead: An icon, a title and one sentence about the page, in two to four columns. The whole card is the link, and screen readers announce the title.

items.title: The whole card is the link
items.description: Each card has one link, and it covers the whole card. There is no second link to the same page.

items.title: A named navigation area
items.description: A page can hold several menus. Screen readers announce this one by its heading, not just as “navigation”.

items.title: The icon is decoration
items.description: A tinted tile with an icon. Screen readers skip it, because the title already says the same.

items.title: Two to four columns
items.description: Editors choose the number of columns. The grid adapts to the space it has, not to the screen width.

items.title: When titles say enough
items.description: If a page needs no description, use a Link Grid instead. It shows the labels without cards.

items.title: Cards of equal height
items.description: Each card stretches to the tallest card in its row, so the icons line up.
